[NX-RUNBOOK-2026]
Title: Focused Nx recovery runbook
Date: 2026-07-08

For Failed to start plugin worker, first run npx nx reset and retry the exact focused command. Keep the test target and flags unchanged so the retry remains comparable. If sandbox restrictions still prevent worker startup, rerun the same focused command with the required approval outside that restriction. Do not widen to a repository-wide test as a substitute.

[WORKTREE-DEPS-2026]
Title: Dependency setup in worktrees
Date: 2026-06-29

A worktree that lacks node_modules should link to the main checkout node_modules before invoking repository scripts. NODE_PATH can help resolution, but the symlink matters because scripts call binaries under the worktree node_modules path. If the branch changes the lockfile or dependencies, the shared install may be stale and must be treated as an environment risk.

[NODE-POLICY-2026]
Title: Supported Node runtime for repository checks
Date: 2026-05-17

Use the repository-pinned Node 22 runtime for Nx, Jest, and TypeScript checks. Failures during plugin initialization under a newer unsupported Node version are environment evidence, not product-test evidence. Record the active version before changing code.

[MAIN-CHECKOUT-PASS-2026]
Title: Comparison run in the main checkout
Date: 2026-07-21

The same focused test target completed in the main checkout with 14 tests passing. This comparison increases confidence that the worktree environment is the immediate problem, but it does not by itself prove that every worktree dependency and configuration matches the main checkout.

[JEST-FAILURE-CATALOG-2026]
Title: Common Jest assertion failures
Date: 2026-04-04

Jest assertion failures include the failing test name, expected and received values, and a stack trace. None of those signals appears when Nx fails before starting its plugin worker.

[REINSTALL-GUIDE-2023]
Title: Archived clean-install troubleshooting
Date: 2023-09-02

This archived generic guide suggests deleting node_modules and the lockfile before reinstalling every dependency. It predates Nx plugin workers and worktree dependency sharing. Repository maintainers no longer use it as the first response to plugin startup failures.

item.text:
This proves Nx failed during startup, before Jest ran. It does not prove that any test, TypeScript code, or product behavior is broken because the output contains no Jest banner, test name, assertion result, or diagnostic [FAILURE-TRACE-2026] [JEST-FAILURE-CATALOG-2026].

Use this verification sequence:

1. **Check the environment.** Confirm the worktree is using the repository-pinned Node 22 runtime [NODE-POLICY-2026]. Verify `node_modules` exists in the worktree and links to the main checkout installation. If the branch changes dependencies or the lockfile, treat that shared installation as potentially stale [WORKTREE-DEPS-2026].

2. **Reset Nx and retry unchanged.** Run `npx nx reset`, then rerun the exact package test command with the same target and flags [NX-RUNBOOK-2026].

3. **Handle execution restrictions narrowly.** If worker startup is still blocked by the sandbox, run that same focused command with the required approval outside the restriction. Do not replace it with repository-wide tests [NX-RUNBOOK-2026].

4. **Report the remaining uncertainty honestly.** The same target passing 14 tests in the main checkout points toward a worktree environment problem, but it does not prove the worktree has matching dependencies or that the branch itself passes [MAIN-CHECKOUT-PASS-2026]. If the focused command still cannot start, record verification as blocked rather than calling the tests failed or passed.

Do not delete `node_modules` or the lockfile as a first step. That advice comes from an archived guide that predates this Nx and worktree setup [REINSTALL-GUIDE-2023].
